name: Two Knights Defense — Traxler Counter-Attack
description: Black ignores the threat to f7 and plays 4...Bc5 (Traxler Counter-Attack / Wilkes-Barre). After 5.Nxf7 Bxf2+!, Black sacs the bishop to drag the white king into the open. Popular surprise weapon on Lichess in club-level games (especially blitz/bullet). Wildly tactical and double-edged.

lines.name: Traxler Counter-Attack
lines.description: The signature Traxler chaos: 4...Bc5 5.Nxf7 Bxf2+! 6.Kxf2 Nxe4+ 7.Ke3 Qh4. White tries 8.g3, but Black has the star shot 8...Nxg3! — the h-pawn is pinned to the rook, so White must recapture 9.hxg3. After 9...Qd4+ 10.Kf3, Black strikes in the center with 10...d5, and White's 11.Rh4 both blocks and counterattacks. Black's initiative rages on.

white.quickTip: Survive the checks and do not grab material — consolidate the exposed king, untangle, and make Black prove the attack.

black.quickTip: Keep checking and creating threats. Do not let White stabilize — use the lead in development and exposed king.
